h1: An Agent SDK for networks that work together

p: An agent is a model, a set of instructions, and the tools it may call. A network is several of them behind a router that decides which one gets the turn — backed by a pure-Rust runtime (hanzoai/dev) and the Hanzo AI gateway (hanzoai/ai).
Open source (hanzoai/agent). pip install hanzo-agent or cargo add hanzo-agent. Works against api.hanzo.ai or any endpoint that speaks Chat Completions and MCP.

li: Add rate limiting to the payments API.
Read 14 files. The limiter belongs in the gateway, not the handler — one place, every route.
Wrote gateway/limit.go and a test at 100 req/min per key. Tests pass.

h2: One agent, or several with a router between them

p: The hard part of multi-agent work is not the prompting. It is deciding who answers, keeping what they learn where the next one can read it, and running tools inside a fast, sandboxed Rust harness.
Built on hanzo-agent (Rust) and the hanzoai/dev Rust harness for sandboxed execution, with first-class SDKs in Rust, Python, Go, and TypeScript (hanzoai/agent).

create_network(agents=[researcher, writer], router=SemanticRouter()) puts specialists behind one call. Route on meaning, on rules you write, or by load — and swap the router without touching the agents.
Every Hanzo MCP tool (260+ tools across files, AST, shell, browser, Kai, and 117 Cloud services) mounts over stdio or streamable HTTP without custom wrappers.

h2: The parts you would otherwise write yourself

p: SemanticRouter reads the request and picks. Rule-based routing does what you say. Load-balanced routing spreads turns across equals. Same network object either way.
Steps that run in parallel, branch on a condition, or loop until something holds — for the work where the order matters and a prompt cannot express it.
Agents in a network read and write one state object, so the writer sees what the researcher found without you pasting it into the next prompt.
A store, a retriever, and vector search over both, so an agent recalls the relevant part of a long history instead of replaying all of it.
Spans and traces around every model call, tool call and handoff, through a processor interface you can point at your own collector.
pip install "hanzo-agent[tee]" adds attestation for confidential runs. [web3] adds wallets and on-chain identity. [cli] adds the command line. Nothing you skip is loaded.

code: # Rust (cargo add hanzo-agent hanzo-agents) · Python (pip install hanzo-agent) from agents import Agent from agents . network import create_network , SemanticRouter researcher = Agent ( name= " Researcher " , instructions= " You find and analyze information. " , tools= [ search_tool , analyze_tool ], ) writer = Agent ( name= " Writer " , instructions= " You create content based on research. " , tools= [ format_tool ], ) network = create_network ( agents= [ researcher , writer ], router=SemanticRouter ()) result = await network . run ( " Research and write about quantum computing " )

p: pip install hanzo-agent, give it instructions and a tool, and run it.
